summary: As of mid-2026, the LLM landscape is dominated by OpenAI's GPT family with ~54% of consumer web traffic, but enterprise API usage tells a different story with Anthropic holding 40% of enterprise API spend versus OpenAI's 27%. Open-source models have surged dramatically, with 79% of developers now using open-weight models according to Mozilla/SlashData surveys, and models from Meta, DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Mistral commanding significant self-hosted deployment. Aggregator reach through AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex has become a critical adoption multiplier, particularly for regulated enterprise sectors that avoid direct vendor APIs.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.1
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT holds 53.9% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits in May 2026 (Similarweb), and OpenAI leads LLM API market share; GPT-5 is available on Azure OpenAI Service, AWS Bedrock, and Snowflake Cortex, massively amplifying enterprise reach beyond direct API numbers.
strengths: Largest consumer mindshare and brand recognition
Multi-step reasoning and conversational depth
Widest aggregator coverage (Azure, AWS Bedrock, Snowflake, Vertex)
Strong tool use and function calling
Real-time interaction capabilities
Massive developer ecosystem and third-party integrations
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise applications, conversational AI, multi-step reasoning workflows, and any team needing the broadest cloud aggregator support

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google Gemini commands 27.9% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits in May 2026 (Similarweb), with web traffic growing ~450% year-over-year to 2.9 billion visits in May 2026; natively integrated into Google Vertex AI and widely available across Google Cloud enterprise deployments.
strengths: Industry-leading 1M token context window
Deep integration with Google Workspace and Google Cloud
Strong multimodal capabilities (text, image, video, audio)
Native Vertex AI availability for enterprise
Excellent performance on coding and reasoning benchmarks
Real-time data access via Google Search grounding
models.best_for: Long-document analysis, multimodal enterprise workflows, and organizations deeply embedded in Google Cloud infrastructure

models.name: Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5.1
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic holds 40% of enterprise API spend (Menlo Ventures 2025), the largest share among all vendors, and Claude recorded 952.6 million web visits in May 2026 (855% YoY growth); available on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, making it the enterprise API leader by spend despite lower consumer web share.
strengths: Highest enterprise API spend share at 40% (Menlo Ventures)
Top-ranked on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
Industry-leading safety and alignment for regulated industries
Exceptional long-context document analysis
Strong coding and complex instruction following
Available on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI
models.best_for: Enterprise applications requiring safety guarantees, long-document processing, complex reasoning, and regulated industry deployments

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Meta Llama 4 is consistently ranked the top open-source model for general reasoning in 2026 and is available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx, giving it unmatched aggregator coverage among open-weight models; 79% of developers now use open-source LLMs (Mozilla/SlashData).
strengths: Fully open weights enabling self-hosting and fine-tuning
Available across all major cloud aggregators (AWS, Azure, Vertex, Snowflake, IBM)
No per-token API costs when self-hosted
Strong general reasoning and instruction following
Large community and extensive fine-tune ecosystem on HuggingFace
Privacy-preserving on-premise deployment option
models.best_for: Organizations requiring on-premise or self-hosted deployment, fine-tuning for domain-specific tasks, and teams needing full data privacy control

models.name: DeepSeek-V3 / DeepSeek-V4
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek holds 4.1% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits (May 2026, Similarweb) and 24.4% of text requests on OpenRouter API marketplace (week of September 21, 2026), signaling extremely high developer API adoption; its cost-efficiency and open-weight availability have driven rapid enterprise uptake globally.
strengths: 24.4% share of OpenRouter API requests among developers
Best-in-class cost efficiency relative to performance
Top-ranked for coding and bug fixing (Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard)
Open weights available for self-hosting
Strong reasoning capabilities via MoE architecture
Developed with significantly less compute than comparable models
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive developer teams, coding assistants, API-heavy applications requiring high throughput at low cost

models.name: Qwen3 / Qwen3-235B
models.popularity_notes: Qwen models have been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises globally (Shakudo) across consumer electronics, gaming, and enterprise sectors; Qwen3-235B-A22B redefined open-weights scale with over 1 trillion total parameters and support for 119 languages, driving massive HuggingFace download volume.
strengths: Adopted by 90,000+ enterprises worldwide
Support for 119 languages with leading multilingual performance
Massive MoE parameter scale (235B total, 22B active)
Strong on coding and reasoning benchmarks
Open weights with active HuggingFace community
Competitive performance against proprietary models at fraction of cost
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise applications, Asian market deployments, and organizations needing large open-weight models for fine-tuning at scale

models.name: Grok-3 / Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Grok holds 2.4% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits (May 2026, Similarweb) with strong growth momentum; its deep integration with X (formerly Twitter) provides a unique real-time data advantage and access to hundreds of millions of X platform users as a built-in distribution channel.
strengths: Real-time data access through X platform integration
Strong performance on math and reasoning benchmarks
Witty and less filtered conversational style
Listed among top 5 LLMs by multiple 2026 ranking sources
Rapidly growing developer API adoption
Competitive on hard reasoning and STEM tasks
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval, social media analytics, and applications requiring up-to-the-minute data grounding

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.popularity_notes: Mistral Large 3 is consistently cited as a top open-source LLM for speed and efficiency in 2026 rankings; available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, and Google Vertex AI, giving it strong enterprise aggregator penetration, while Mixtral MoE architecture underpins many enterprise cost-optimized deployments.
strengths: Best-in-class inference speed among large open models
MoE architecture for cost-efficient high-throughput deployments
Available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, and Google Vertex AI
Strong European data sovereignty compliance
Low latency for real-time applications
Active open-source community with extensive fine-tune support
models.best_for: High-throughput production applications, latency-sensitive APIs, European enterprises with data residency requirements

models.name: Microsoft Copilot (GPT-5 powered)
models.popularity_notes: Microsoft Copilot holds 1.3% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits (May 2026, Similarweb), but its true adoption is vastly larger via embedded integration in Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook) used by 400M+ commercial seats, making it one of the most widely deployed AI assistants measured by active enterprise users.
strengths: Embedded in Microsoft 365 suite with 400M+ commercial seats
Deep integration with Azure OpenAI Service for enterprise customization
Native GitHub Copilot for code generation widely adopted by developers
Strong enterprise security and compliance framework
Seamless SharePoint, Teams, and Outlook workflow automation
Available across Azure, Snowflake Cortex via Azure OpenAI
models.best_for: Microsoft 365 enterprise environments, developer productivity via GitHub Copilot, and organizations standardized on Azure infrastructure

models.name: Perplexity AI
models.popularity_notes: Perplexity holds 1.3% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits (May 2026, Similarweb), with rapid growth driven by its search-augmented LLM approach that routes queries through multiple underlying models (GPT-5, Claude, Sonar); it has become a primary research and information retrieval tool for developer and knowledge-worker segments.
strengths: Real-time web search grounding with cited sources
Multi-model routing (GPT-5, Claude, Sonar) in single interface
Strong adoption among developers and researchers for information retrieval
Sonar API enables search-augmented generation for product builders
Low hallucination rate due to live web retrieval
Fast response times with inline citations
models.best_for: Research-intensive workflows, real-time fact-checked content generation, and developer applications requiring search-augmented generation with citations
